notes: dc CALL 2026-10-21: Q3 2026 earnings call (CEO Zuckerberg, CFO Li); transcript from Alpha Vantage EARNINGS_CALL_TRANSCRIPT 2026Q3, one call, saved to gather/raw_documents/av_EARNINGS_CALL_TRANSCRIPT_META_2026Q3.json (text in transcript_META_2026Q3.txt). A provider copy of the issuer call, so not independent. Release (2026-10-21) and 10-Q (2026-10-22) are citable at as_of 2026-10-27 (LAG_DAYS 2).
dc CITABILITY the results of 2026-10-21 are 6 days old, so release, call and 10-Q can back drivers, events and the key risk; the Class C stock dividend record and payment dates are not yet set.

dc RESULT Q3 2026 revenue 64.601B +26% (+26% constant currency), advertising 63.061B +26%, FoA other revenue 1.097B +59% (WhatsApp paid messaging, subscriptions), Reality Labs 443M -6%. Impressions +10%, price per ad +14%, DAP 3.64B +3%, ARPP 17.72 +23% (pf_rel_20261021_1, pf_10q_20261022, call).

dc RESULT costs and expenses 51.613B +68% include a 9.89B charge for the August 2026 agreement with 52 attorneys general (G&A line). Operating income 12.988B (20% margin) vs 20.535B; ex-charge 22.88B (company arithmetic), +11% y/y per the CFO. Diluted EPS 3.83; ex-charge 7.40 (company arithmetic). Tax rate 24% (above outlook) because of the nondeductible part of legal expense; 17% ex-charge.

dc ONEOFF prior-year comparatives: Q3 2025 net income 2.709B carried a 15.93B discrete tax charge on enactment of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (effective tax rate 87%); Q1 2026 had an 8.03B discrete tax benefit from CAMT transitional relief (Treasury Notice 2026-7); 9M 2026 tax rate 2%. Reported net income and EPS growth (+264%) is therefore not a clean comparison.

dc ONEOFF legal charges recur as a category: 2.4B charges in Q2 2026 (pf_rel_20260729_1), 9.89B in Q3 2026, legal-related accruals 11.577B current and 8.304B non-current at 2026-09-30, 5.3B contingent AG amount not accrued, 1.18B severance in 9M 2026 (May 2026 reduction of about 8,000 employees). Operating income ex the AG charge is not a run rate that excludes legal costs.

dc AGREEMENT the AG settlement: payments up to about 18.59B, of which about 12.7B payable in annual installments over 10 years and about 5.3B contingent amounts not accrued; includes about 500M for the privacy matters (pf_rel_20261021_1, pf_10q_20261022 Notes 8 and 10, liquidity section).

dc COMMIT contractual commitments: 454.52B non-cancelable (mostly third-party cloud capacity, servers and network, energy service agreements, Reality Labs hardware), 45.85B due remainder of 2026 and 121.41B due 2027; plus leases not yet commenced 355.73B (start remainder of 2026 through 2036, terms 1 to 30 years); contingent cloud purchase up to 14.72B over five years (pf_10q_20261022 Note 10). No fixed RPO or backlog exists (advertising; deferred revenue 1.19B).

dc COMMIT data center ventures (Louisiana and Texas, unconsolidated): maximum exposure to loss 68.404B = equity carrying value 4.732B + lease commitments 18.476B + future funding 3.703B + residual value guarantees 41.493B (31 Dec 2025: 45.952B). Leases commence 2028 (Texas) and 2029 (Louisiana). A claim ahead of the shares the debt lines miss; the analyst decides whether to treat the RVG as debt-like (pf_10q_20261022 Note 5).

dc LIQUIDITY cash and marketable securities 82.45B (cash 11.222B + securities 71.227B) as of 2026-09-30; restricted cash and equivalents 13.132B (597M current + 12.535B non-current; 10.80B is escrow for multi-year infrastructure purchase agreements, released 2028-2030) is not spendable liquidity. Debt face 84.0B (carrying 83.669B incl 2.747B current; fair value 73.31B); May 2026 issue of 25.0B senior notes at 4.55-6.45%; principal due 2.75B 2027, 1.5B 2028, 1.0B 2029, 5.0B 2030, 73.75B thereafter. No financial covenants. Notes interest expense net of capitalized 882M in Q3 2026 vs 205M.

dc CASHFLOW Q3 2026 operating cash flow 32.786B, purchases of property and equipment 33.942B plus finance lease principal 0.964B (capex incl finance leases 34.91B), company-defined free cash flow -2.12B; 9M free cash flow 11.049B vs 29.508B. No repurchases in 9M 2026 (25.03B authorization remains); dividends 0.525 per share quarterly (1.361B). Taxes paid on net share settlement 4.064B in Q3.

dc SHARES Class A 2,214,472,367 and Class B 341,768,886 outstanding at 2026-10-16 (total 2.556B); diluted weighted average 2,573M in Q3 2026 (2,572M a year earlier). New Class C non-voting stock: charter effective 2027-01-19, one-time stock dividend of one Class C per Class A or B share (economically a two-for-one split; per-share history to be restated retroactively); stated purposes: capital raising, employee compensation, acquisitions. CFO on the call: no specific financing plans to announce (pf_rel_20261021_1, pf_10q_20261022 Note 14, call).

dc GUIDE FY2026 total expenses 175-179B raised from 165-169B (July) only to include the 9.89B charge; capex 135-145B narrowed from 130-145B (it was 115-135B in January, 125-145B in April); Reality Labs loss 18-19B (FY2025 loss 19.193B); Q4 2026 tax rate 15-17%; FY2026 operating income expected above 2025 excluding the Q3 legal charge (qualitative, FY2025 operating income 83.276B); RL loss around 15B in 2027. No full-year 2027 revenue or expense outlook (the Q4 call, usually February, gives 2027 guidance).

dc GUIDE derived, not guided: 9M 2026 revenue 181.712B plus the Q4 guide 73-76B implies FY2026 revenue 254.7-257.7B (+26.7% to +28.2% on FY2025 200.966B); FY2026 expenses 175-179B less 9M 127.077B implies Q4 expenses 47.9-51.9B and Q4 operating income of roughly 21-28B; the Q4 revenue guide midpoint 74.5B is +24% on Q4 2025 59.893B with about 1 point of currency headwind.

dc GUIDE track: Q3 2026 revenue guided 61-64B (2026-07-29) and delivered 64.601B, above the top of the range; Q2 guided 58-61B delivered 60.801B; Q1 guided 53.5-56.5B delivered 56.311B (all from the releases; ticker-check prints the ratio for the pack track).

dc MGMT (statements, not facts) 2027: revenue growth 'to sustain strong overall revenue growth throughout 2027' because of AI gains in the core business and new AI products; 'continue investing aggressively'; capacity plans still being developed with the 2027 budget and expense and capex outlook only at the Q4 call; CEO/CFO on the call: new AI businesses 'can begin contributing incremental revenue in 2027'.

dc MGMT Muse (personal agent, frontier model Muse Wonder): more than 10M set up in US and Canada in about six weeks, about 25% use it on a given day, more than 25% of users engage in shopping with average purchase over 200 USD; not launched globally mostly because of compute intensity; monetization to start sooner than the usual playbook: free tier, commerce fee paid by businesses, subscriptions for advanced models, business subscriptions, a model API and Muse Code. CEO: serving cost efficiency expected to improve more than 10x in the next year; Muse profitable only once revenue lines are at scale; the CFO gave no per-user cost.

dc MGMT core ads: CFO attributes engagement and monetization gains to ranking and recommendation models (Instagram Reels time spent +4% from Q3 launches, Facebook generative retrieval, Andromeda +1.4% conversions, JEM +1.7% off-site and +9.6% app conversions), partnership ads over 15B run rate and +97% y/y, nearly 10M advertisers on generative creative tools, Meta One subscriptions and trials above 15M; price per ad growth partly offset by growth of lower-monetizing surfaces and regions.

dc MGMT Reality Labs: loss to narrow to about 15B in 2027 as VR device launches are paced and investment moves to AI; glasses sales growing fast, hardware priced for software and subscription revenue; CEO: operating loss 'trending toward profitability from there' (no date).

dc MGMT cost and headcount: headcount 66,775 (-15% y/y; -12% from Q2 after the May 2026 reduction); Q3 expense growth driven by legal costs, infrastructure (third-party cloud, depreciation, data center operating costs) and third-party AI token costs.

dc KPI revenue growth by user geography in Q3 2026 (10-Q MD&A): US and Canada +33%, Europe +18%, Asia-Pacific +16%, Rest of World +34%; revenue by customer address is in the 10-Q Note 2 (gather_macro owns geography). ARPP quarter series in the 10-Q chart text is nine values Q3 2024 to Q3 2026; only the last (17.72, +23%) is stated in words, the earlier positions are inferred from order and the 23% growth check (17.72 / 14.46).

dc KPI identity: ARPP is Family of Apps revenue divided by the average of beginning and end DAP; 17.72 x average of June and September 2026 DAP (3.60B, 3.64B) is about 64.1B, matching FoA revenue 64.158B. DAP carries an estimate margin of about 3% and counts people not accounts; slight Q1 2026 decline from Iran internet disruptions and a WhatsApp restriction in Russia.

dc CUSTOMERS no customer represented 10% or more of revenue or accounts receivable in 2025, 2024 and 2023 (10-K notes); millions of advertisers, no long-term advertising commitments (Item 1A), so the customers list is empty by design.

dc RISK 1 advertising dependence: substantially all revenue is advertising on Facebook and Instagram; marketers have no long-term commitments and can cut spend quickly (10-Q Item 1A, 'We generate substantially all of our revenue from advertising').

dc RISK 2 youth-related litigation: AG agreement of up to 18.59B, 5.3B contingent not accrued; first school district bellwether settled May 2026, next trial February 2027; mass arbitration demands from over 200,000 claimants; damages sought have at times been above one trillion dollars; further youth trials scheduled in the coming months (10-Q Note 10, CFO outlook).

dc RISK 3 EU regulation: DMA decision on 'subscription for no ads' (200M euro fine, April 2025, appealed), less personalized ads changes that 'could result in a significant impact to our European business and revenue'; DSA preliminary findings (October 2025); Marketplace Article 102 fine of about 798M euro under appeal; Europe was 14.0B of Q3 revenue by customer address, 22% (10-Q Notes 2 and 10).

dc RISK 4 AI and infrastructure spend: 2026 capex 135-145B, Q3 free cash flow negative, 454.52B non-cancelable commitments and 355.73B leases not yet commenced, investments in AI and Reality Labs reduce cash flow, margin and profitability and may not pay back (10-Q Item 1A, 'We incur significant expenses' and 'We may not be successful in our artificial intelligence initiatives', Note 10).

dc RISK 5 technical infrastructure and supply: a substantial portion of infrastructure is provided by third parties (cloud capacity), disruptions or component price increases hit capacity and cost; capex guide was raised in April on higher component pricing; consumer hardware has design, manufacturing and inventory risk (10-Q Item 1A; pf_rel_20260429_1).

dc RISK 6 competition and platform dependence: the business is highly competitive for users' time and advertisers' budgets, and ad targeting and measurement rely on data signals and mobile operating systems and networks Meta does not control; government restrictions on access in countries (10-Q Item 1A).

dc RISK 7 tax: effective rate volatile (87% in Q3 2025, 2% in 9M 2026, 24% in Q3 2026); gross unrecognized tax benefits 20.82B; transfer-pricing Tax Court matter; CAMT limits some deductions in 2026; changes in tax law (10-Q Note 12 and Item 1A).

dc RISK 8 control and capital structure: Class B (ten votes) gives the CEO majority voting control, controlled company status; the Class C non-voting stock widens funding tools (equity raise, acquisitions, compensation) and is a dilution channel for current holders (10-Q Item 1A, Note 14, release).

dc SOURCES the 10-K (2026-01-29) was read for customer concentration only; RPO or backlog: none disclosed for an advertising model; purchase commitments are from the 10-Q (more recent than the 10-K). The 10-Q chart values for DAP, ad impressions and price per ad by region are images and are not in the saved text.

dc EQUITY RAISE (new since the 2026-10-27 run; sources dc_s3asr_20261026, dc_fwp_launch_20261026, dc_fwp_pricing_20261026, dc_424b5_*_20261028, dc_8k_20261029; all citable, last dated 2026-10-29): on 2026-10-26 Meta filed an automatic shelf (S-3ASR, Reg. 333-299631) and priced two concurrent offerings, trade date 2026-10-27, settlement 2026-10-29: (1) 40,000,000 Class A shares at 625.00 (25.0B gross; last sale 630.56 on 10-26) sold by forward sellers, NOT issued now, no cash at closing; (2) 250,000,000 Series A depositary shares at 50.00 = 12.5B (12.5M preferred shares, 1,000 liquidation preference), closed 2026-10-29, net about 12.458B before about 4M expenses. The launch FWP first sized the common at 22.5B; the pricing term sheet increased it to 25.0B (46M shares / 28.7B net if the 6M-share option is fully exercised); the preferred has a 37.5M-depositary-share (1.875B) over-allotment option, 30 days from 10-26. No filing in the saved list says whether either option was exercised: unknown.

dc EQUITY FORWARD TERMS: two forward purchasers (Morgan Stanley Capital Services, Goldman Sachs) each hold a forward on part of the 40M shares; settlement date or dates at Meta's discretion on or before 2027-11-19; initial forward price 622.91875 (625.00 less 2.08125 discount, 83.25M), adjusted daily by a floating rate (overnight bank funding rate less a spread) and reduced on specified dates by amounts tied to expected dividends; expected net proceeds about 24.9B at settlement (about 28.7B with the option), general corporate purposes; shares are treated as potential dilution under the treasury stock method until settlement. Once Class C stock exists (charter effective 2027-01-19) the forwards split into Class A and Class C transactions and Meta may settle in Class C only, with a price reduction tied to the A/C trading gap. Forward purchasers may accelerate settlement on stock-borrow failure, a dividend above a set amount, ownership thresholds, extraordinary events or defaults.

dc EQUITY PREFERRED TERMS: 6.50% cumulative Series A mandatory convertible preferred (depositary shares METAM, Nasdaq), dividends 6.50% of 1,000 = 65.00 per preferred share per year (0.8125 per depositary share; about 812.5M a year on 12.5B), payable quarterly (Feb 15, May 15, Aug 15, Nov 15) from 2027-02-15 to 2029-08-15 in cash, Class A shares or a mix at the board's choice (first payment about 19.1389 per preferred share). Mandatory conversion about 2029-08-15 into 1.3620 to 1.6000 Class A shares per preferred share (0.0681 to 0.0800 per depositary share): initial price 625.00, threshold appreciation price 734.2144 (+17.5%), floor price 218.75; at a 20-day average price above 734.21 holders get 1.3620 shares (about 17.0M shares in all), below 625 they get 1.6000 (about 20.0M shares); conversion into Class C possible after Class C exists. While preferred is outstanding with unpaid dividends no common dividend or buyback is allowed (limited exceptions; binding buyback contracts in place before issue are carved out). Liquidation: greater of 1,000 plus accrued dividends or as-converted value, senior to common. Derived from the terms: 12.5B x (1.3620 to 1.6000)/1,000 = 17.0M to 20.0M Class A shares; 40M forward shares against 2,214.455M Class A (2,556M total with Class B at 2026-10-16) is about 1.6% of total shares; both together up to 60M shares about 2.3% (company arithmetic not given; derived here).

dc EQUITY FINANCING PLAN (dc_fwp_launch_20261026, issuer statement, not a fact until it happens): the launch release calls these offerings part of a financing plan: about 35B of underwritten equity now (22.5B common + 12.5B preferred at launch; common later raised to 25.0B, about 37.5B total) plus a PLANNED at-the-market program of about 60B once the Class C stock begins trading; no ATM agreement exists, and timing, size and terms are undetermined. Management says it funds the 135-145B 2026 capex through 'a balanced mix of operating cash flow, investment-grade debt, strategic partnerships, and equity capital'; cites 97B operating cash flow in 9M 2026, about 82B cash and securities at Q3 end, Aa3/AA- ratings, total consolidated indebtedness 83.7B at 2026-09-30 (prospectus). Use of proceeds: general corporate purposes only. Together the identified equity is about 37.5B now (12.5B received 10-29, about 24.9B after forward settlement) and up to about 60B more through the ATM: the analyst must carry this funding and current-holder dilution into the forecast (CLAUDE.md rule) and test the share count, not use the 2.573B diluted figure unchanged.

dc EQUITY CITABILITY the 8-K of 2026-10-29 is citable from 2026-10-31, the 424B5s of 2026-10-28 from 2026-10-30, the FWPs and S-3ASR earlier: all citable at as_of 2026-11-01. The S-3ASR is a pay-as-you-go automatic shelf with no stated maximum amount (registration fee deferred), so it does not itself cap further issuance. Raw copies are in gather/raw_documents/ (sec_8k_20261029.*, final_436410_fwd.*, final_436405_pref.*, d382225dfwp.*, d116268dfwp.*, d127909ds3asr.*; prelim_* names were overwritten by same-name files from other accessions and are not kept).

dc RISK 9 dilution and funding (new): equity raise of about 37.5B (preferred 12.5B closed, common 25.0B forward) plus a planned about 60B ATM, a 6.50% preferred that blocks common dividends and buybacks while unpaid, and the Class C charter effective 2027-01-19; these respond to negative Q3 free cash flow and 135-145B capex (dc_fwp_launch_20261026, dc_424b5_*).
gaps: No company-reported Reality Labs unit KPIs (glasses units, Quest units) in the documents; AI glasses growth is only described in words on the call.
Per-user Muse compute cost, Muse revenue and the monetization timetable are not given by management (CFO: no specific numbers).
DAP, impressions and price per ad by region are charts in the 10-Q and did not survive in the saved text; only worldwide figures and revenue growth by user geography are available.
FY2027 revenue, expense and capex outlook not given until the Q4 2026 call; no explicit FY2026 revenue guide (derived from 9M actual plus the Q4 guide).
Q3 2026 10-Q segment line for AG charge allocation: the charge sits in Family of Apps costs (G&A), the exact segment attribution is not broken out beyond the 10-Q segment table.

Whether the underwriters' options (6M Class A shares, 37.5M depositary shares) were exercised is not in the filings saved (no 8-K or 424B after 2026-10-29); the preferred closing amount quoted is the base 12.5B.
ATM program (about 60B) is only an intention in the launch FWP: no agreement, size or timing; not yet a fact.

The Q3 10-Q (filed 2026-10-22) predates the raise: its share count (2.556B at 2026-10-16) and balance sheet (cash 82.45B) do not include the 12.5B preferred proceeds; the equity raise is a subsequent event not in the quarter-review case balance.
